agree.reason: A warm, clear ask, but it gives an editor with a $9,000 budget and an $8,000 newer illustrator nothing besides past sales to justify $2,500 more: no schedule commitment, no spot drawings and no fourth printing.

honest.reason: It drops the unsupported claim that every other publisher pays at least $12,000 and keeps to the real figures, though 'my fees outside our work have gone up' rests on a single $12,500 book.

works_the_facts.reason: It restates the figures but works none of them out, such as $9,000 over four months being about $2,250 a month or $11,500 being $1,000 under her own outside rate, and it leaves out the fourth printing, the sketch timeline and the September 1 delivery.

right_comparison.reason: The only comparison is with another publisher; the editor's real alternative, a cheaper but unproven illustrator against a record of two 20,000-copy books still being reprinted, is never addressed.

qualification.reason: It names no checkable commitment such as sketches within six weeks of signing or final art by September 1, and it doesn't acknowledge the end-of-next-week deadline, so the only conditional is a vague 'can no longer set aside that much time'.

objections.reason: The budget-and-cheaper-option objection isn't met with added value or a reason the proven sales outweigh $3,500, and asking Nadia to 'take this to whoever needs to approve it' misreads who makes the decision.

fit.reason: A properly formatted email of about 200 words, well under the limit, though it still ends with the '[Your name]' placeholder even though the name was known.
